Sound the downgrade siren, or park it when another alarm owns the bus. There is one alarm thread (shared_alarm_start refuses a second). Parking is scoped to quality_downgrade, promoted by the supervision tick, and expires after QUALITY_PENDING_MAX_WAIT_SEC into an explicit log line. Silently dropping the alarm is what BUG-029 was reported as. A quality alarm never parks behind another quality alarm: the siren is already ringing for the same condition, so the call is a no-op (BLOCKER 2).

Tick: promote a parked downgrade once the bus frees, or say it was withheld. Promotion is refused when the operator already acknowledged these params while the alarm was parked (BLOCKER 2 item 7) and when the parking window expired.

Regression checks for BUG-012 retained-backup renewal scheduling. Covers the five hunks approved for Stage 3B in ``Recorder-Docs/SPECIFICATIONS/2026-10-25_BUG-012_RETAINED_BACKUP_POLLING_3A_SPEC_OUT_R2.md``: the renewal card tells the truth about the next check, a discarded backup re-arms the clock at once, and a backup that expires while a check is in progress is dropped the same way through both doors. Also covers the Round 1 audit remediations approved for Stage 5B and carried in ``..._3B_SPEC_OUT_R3.md``: the backup and the candidate pool are judged at a clock read taken *after* the quality probes (TD-1, TD-1b), the successful door reports a lost backup at ``WARN`` like the failed door (P-1), and the discard-then-scan ordering inside one pass is proven rather than inferred (P-3, audit §6.4). The recorder reads machine-specific configuration at import time, so each hunk is compiled from ``record_dynamic.py``'s AST and executed against stub globals. No recorder, network, or thread is started.

Run the §3.4 block with the scan clock and the probe clock apart. ``scan_time`` is the ``check_time`` sample taken before the quality probes; ``probe_clock`` is what ``time.time()`` returns when the block runs after them. They differ only in TD-1's window.
# Item 3: the ACK key carries the standard's rate, not the missing 0.0.
A recovered chunk silences the siren and re-arms the next real drop (BLOCKER 1).
An fps=0 startup reading defers once and never locks out the probe (Item 5).
EXPECTED_VIDEO without a frame rate inherits the learned one (Item 6).

R1: ack, then a long gap with no sweeper tick, then a cut starts a fresh episode. The acknowledgement stamps its quiet window from the real clock (BUG-032), so the synthetic cut times are offsets from time.monotonic() rather than absolute constants - otherwise the "31 minutes later" cut lands inside a quiet window that was opened in the present.

R2: a cut after 'A' is beep-only while the five-minute quiet window is open. The acknowledgement stamps its quiet window from the real clock (BUG-032), so the cut times are offsets from time.monotonic() rather than absolute constants. With constants this test silently depended on how long the host had been up: on a freshly booted runner (CI) 5200.0 was already past the window, the siren re-armed and the "later cut only beeps" expectation failed.

Verifies Item 5: Dynamic summary report header and failure propagation: 1. Summary header distinguishes mixed params from assembly failures. 2. finalize_recording sets state.last_finalization_failure on failure.

Verifies Item 8: Complete parity between record_static.py and record_dynamic.py for: 1. MIN_ACCEPTED_CHUNK_SECONDS = 60 2. quality_downgrade alarm functions and state fields 3. Two-tier duration acceptance and short downgrade discard logic 4. Headless terminal key listener error handling
